verifications.claim: The Artemis program is a series of NASA-led missions returning humans to the Moon for long-term exploration.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Under Artemis, NASA will send astronauts on increasingly difficult missions to explore more of the Moon... long-term return to the Moon'; R3: 'Moon exploration program led by... NASA... aimed at returning humans to the Moon... sustainable crewed lunar exploration'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches descriptions of NASA-led program for sustained lunar human exploration.

verifications.claim: Artemis I successfully completed an uncrewed test flight on November 16, 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I Launched in 2022'; R3: 'Artemis I (November 16, 2022)'; R4: 'Artemis 1... took place in November and December 2022'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date and uncrewed success confirmed across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis I tested the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I was the first... test flight of the SLS... and Orion'; R3: 'first uncrewed test flight of the SLS, Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states testing SLS and Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis I orbited the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'sent an Orion spacecraft to lunar orbit'; R4: 'orbited 130 km above the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of lunar orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is targeted for April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Launch date April 1, 2026'; R3: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026)'; R4: 'Artemis 2 launched on 1 April 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm exact launch in April 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft to orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'crewed lunar flyby mission... did not enter lunar orbit'; R3: 'lunar fly-by'
verifications.reasoning: Mission was a flyby, explicitly not entering lunar orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will last ~10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mission duration 9 days, 1 hour... approximately ten-day trip'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: '10-day expedition'
verifications.reasoning: ~10 days directly matches reported duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will test life-support and emergency systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'crew evaluated life support... critical spacecraft systems'; R5: 'test life support systems'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit testing of life-support systems described.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is targeted for mid-2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Scheduled for 2027'; R3: 'mid-2027'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for mid-2027 target.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is targeted to land the first astronauts on the lunar South Pole.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III... demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test... commercial landers'; R3: 'test of HLS in Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: No landing planned for Artemis III; it's Earth orbit test.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will include the first woman and first person of color among those astronauts.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Victor Glover... first person of color, Christina Koch the first woman' (for Artemis II); R3: 'TBA' for Artemis III crew
verifications.reasoning: Milestones achieved on Artemis II, not III; III crew unspecified.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will use a SpaceX HLS (Human Landing System).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'; R3: 'one or both... SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon'
verifications.reasoning: SpaceX HLS is one option among possibly both, not exclusively confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is targeted for early 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA continues to target early 2028'; R3: 'early 2028'
verifications.reasoning: Exact target date confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is a second crewed landing mission.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first Artemis lunar landing'; R3: 'first lunar landing of the program'
verifications.reasoning: Described as the first landing, not second.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV will carry out construction of the Gateway.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Lunar Gateway program was cancelled in March 2026'; previously planned but changed
verifications.reasoning: Gateway cancelled; no construction on Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: The Gateway is an orbiting lunar space station.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Lunar Gateway was a planned space station that would have been assembled in orbit around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Accurate description despite cancellation.

verifications.claim: Artemis V is targeted for late 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch this lunar surface mission by late 2028'; R3: 'late 2028'
verifications.reasoning: Direct target confirmation.

verifications.claim: Artemis V involves further lunar surface missions to build a permanent base.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lunar surface mission'; R3: 'second lunar landing... begin building its Moon base'
verifications.reasoning: Matches plans for surface mission and base construction.

verifications.claim: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Crew... Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen'; R3, R4 same
verifications.reasoning: Exact Artemis II crew listed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launch uses SLS from Kennedy Space Center, FL, placing Orion in Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Rocket Space Launch System... Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B... placing the spacecraft into a stable low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Precise details match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II includes translunar injection where engines fire to send Orion toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'trans-lunar injection (TLI) burn... placed the spacecraft on a free-return trajectory'; R5: 'translunar injection burn'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described.

verifications.claim: Artemis II includes a lunar flyby where the crew loops around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'lunar flyby... looping around the far side'; R3: 'lunar fly-by... swing around the far side'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II return involves a slingshot maneuver and splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'free-return trajectory... slingshot maneuver... splashdown... Pacific Ocean'; R4: 'slingshot back... splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly describes return phase.
